A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and retain matching methods and experiments. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original detection experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, including adaptive attacks and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v5.pdf retains these original results and adds experiments on adaptive attacks, Transformers, system operating points and benign noise.

M1.justification: The core RT, LT and RLT formulas and Algorithm 1 are retained. v5 adds a ViT adaptation using aggregated patch strips and token chunks with 80 recovery modules (Appendix F), plus a threshold-selection procedure that maximizes system-accuracy lower bounds (Appendix H). These extend the existing detector without replacing its scoring method.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet remain; CIFAR-100 was already evaluated in v1 Appendix D. v5 adds explicit L2-PGD, detector-aware query-only SimBA, and prediction-preserving random-noise scenarios. These expand testing conditions within the existing vision task.

E2.justification: Comparator sets in retained Tables 2–4 are unchanged. New comparisons include Mao and BEYOND in the end-to-end PGD tables, LID in the ViT evaluation, and undefended classifiers in SimBA/system evaluations. Appendix G also adds resource comparisons using BYOL, SimSiam and MoCo v3.

E3.justification: v5 adds fused-score PGD with three lambda values, 1,000-query SimBA, ViT and adversarially trained classifier configurations, and system metrics across operating points. The retained single-objective ablation is also described differently: v1 C.4 removes attacker objectives while retaining RLT detection, whereas v5 D.4 removes components from both attacker and defender. Its unchanged numerical table establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds mismatched attack/defense objectives (Table 13), L2-norm robustness (D.7), benign-noise specificity (I), and extensive cost/performance and system operating-point analyses (G–H). Earlier recovery-size, augmentation-count, layer-selection, perturbation-budget and score-term ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs in Table 2. v5 extends this existing convention to new PGD results; it does not introduce a different repeated-run policy, seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in v1's original result tables are retained. Substantial new results include end-to-end PGD RA of 20.72 ± 8.04% at 5% FPR for lambda=1 (v5 Table 5), SimBA RA of 97.62% versus 5.54% undefended (Table 7), and ViT, L2, noise, resource and system results. These are additional experimental conditions rather than improvements to the retained scores.

T1.justification: The original assumptions, four detection theorems and proofs are retained. v5 adds a local layer-wise Lipschitz definition and its connection to reconstruction errors (B.1), system-performance relationships, and Theorems 5–6 with proofs establishing accuracy lower bounds for unknown or bounded attack probabilities (H).

C1.justification: v5 claims priority for formalizing internal disruptions as layer-wise Lipschitz violations and makes threshold selection with accuracy lower bounds a central contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. The abstract also drops v1's unqualified claim of no compromise to clean accuracy.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations of clean-accuracy/robustness trade-offs, benefits with adversarially trained classifiers, and benign-noise specificity. It interprets SimBA results as ruling out gradient masking and reframes the single-objective ablation as demonstrating insufficient individual components. Conversely, the shortened limitations discussion removes v1's specific warning about overlapping intermediate/logit distortions and reduces its discussion of LT as a coarse sensitivity proxy.

D1.justification: v5 supplies a code-repository link, discloses identity initialization of LT transformations, and newly describes BPDA handling of quantile normalization. Appendix F details ViT feature aggregation and recovery-module construction, while Appendix G supplies architecture and parameter configurations. The original AdamW, batch-size, training-epoch and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds the obfuscated-gradients/BPDA and SimBA references and removes the Attention Is All You Need reference. It also adds specific novelty positioning around Lipschitz formalization and a claimed gap in prior system-level analysis. The broader detector literature and related-work taxonomy remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially revised around the new formalization and system analysis. Related work moves from the main text to Appendix A, Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix J, and the standalone limitations section becomes a short conclusion paragraph. The appendices are extensively reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and the original tables are retained with repositioning and reflow. v5 adds substantial new displays, including PGD operating-point tables, an attack/defense matrix, a ViT comparison, extensive resource grids, and system/noise tables. These materially expand the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens validation through fused-score adaptive PGD with documented BPDA, query-only attacks, and ViT experiments addressing v1's explicit CNN-only limitation. Appendix H measures clean-accuracy costs and analyzes operating points absent from v1, making practical performance more assessable. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed failure-mode warnings, although the claim that SimBA completely rules out gradient masking is stronger than that experiment establishes.
